title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Amberfield Bank
summary: Weekly POC security sync to review SSO progress, audit log retention and format, data retention/deletion during pilot, and SOC 2 evidence requests. Redwood clarified SAML/SCIM flow, KMS options, and provided timeline for audit log export. Customer requested sample audit-log schema, end-to-end SSO test steps, and confirmation of data purging after POC.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share SSO step-by-step checklist and demo account details (due 2026-11-13)
Priya Shah: Export example audit log schema + sample 7-day export (due 2026-11-12)
Maya Ortiz: Provide SOC 2 interim report and scope doc (due 2026-11-16)
Elena Ruiz: Provide list of internal compliance reviewers and preferred evidence format (due 2026-11-18)
Mark Thompson: Schedule SSO test window and confirm AD side contacts (due 2026-11-15)
next_steps: Redwood to send SAML metadata and SCIM provisioning instructions
Redwood to provide sample audit log export and mapping to Amberfield SIEM fields
Amberfield to schedule a 60-min SSO test with infra team next week
Plan a SOC 2 evidence handoff after Redwood shares interim report
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-11-11 15:00 PST | 45 minutes | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Maya (Redwood); Mark, Elena, David, Sara (Amberfield)
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — sso status, audit logs, data retention, soc2 ask, then next steps.
[00:35] Mark Thompson: Yeah thanks Jordan. We did a first pass on SAML last night, but we hit a couple of issues with the metadata exchange, so hoping we can nail that down.
[01:10] Priya Shah: ok good, quick note — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. most customers do SP-initiated first; we'll send metadata and a checklist after this call.
[02:05] Elena Ruiz: for provisioning we need the SCIM user schema to map groups to roles. are groups preserved from our AD sync? sometimes SCIM mapping gets fuzzy.

[03:00] Priya Shah: yes, we map groups via the SCIM group object, but small caveat — if you use nested groups, that's where mapping can vary. we'll include examples. also note there was a transcribe earlier where KV cache was transcribed as KV cash in a doc — ignore that :)
[05:20] David Kim: on audit logs: what fields do you include and can we export in a syslog/JSON format to our SIEM? we need timestamp, user id, action, model id, route, and token counts ideally.

[06:05] Priya Shah: we produce structured JSON events. standard fields are event_time, user_email, request_id, model, latency_ms, token_in, token_out, route, and decision flags. can export via S3 or push to your syslog via forwarder. we'll attach sample schema.
[07:30] Sara Ng: retention during the POC — we want logs stored for 90 days but need a way to auto-delete/expire after pilot ends. also any PII redaction options?

[08:15] Jordan Lee: by default hosted retains logs for 30 days, Dedicated can be configured longer. for POC we can provision a 90-day bucket and then schedule an automated purge after the POC end date. PII — we can mask user content and configure redaction rules but we'd need to validate with your compliance team.
[10:40] Elena Ruiz: encryption at rest — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for the POC or only Redwood-managed keys?

[11:05] Priya Shah: for hosted POC we support Redwood-managed KMS; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS or HSM integration. we can do an interim arrangement where audit logs are encrypted with a customer key in an S3 bucket we provisioned for the POC.
[13:20] Mark Thompson: that would work. we also want to see how keys rotate — do you rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation windows?

[14:00] Priya Shah: rotation is automatic for Redwood-managed keys; for customer-managed keys you control rotation in your KMS, and we accept the key ARN. we'll document the rotation requirement in the security playbook.
[17:10] David Kim: SOC 2 — we need evidence around change control and access logs for engineers who touch the infra. do you have a SOC 2 interim report or scope we can review?

[18:00] Maya Ortiz: yes, we have a SOC 2 type II report for our control plane and can share a redacted interim report plus the control matrix. i'll attach the scope doc and point to evidence buckets. note: some evidence requires an NDA/secure share.
[20:25] Sara Ng: ok great. can you also include who on Redwood's side handles incident response and SOC escalation contacts?
[21:05] Jordan Lee: yes will include primary on-call and escalation path. also, keep in mind that for Dedicated/private deployments we can integrate with your ticketing and incident workflow.
[24:40] Mark Thompson: small question on data deletion — if we delete a dataset or conversation during the POC, does it purge from all caches and backups immediately or on a retention schedule?

[25:10] Priya Shah: deletion triggers will remove items from the active KV cache and mark it for deletion from storage; backups adhere to retention windows and may persist for a short time until the next snapshot window. we'll document exact timing and offer an option to forcibly expire snapshots for the POC.
[28:00] Elena Ruiz: can we get an SLA for audit-log availability? we need logs to be available for ingestion within 2 minutes of event for monitoring.
[28:30] Priya Shah: typical ingestion lag is sub-60s but we can validate under your workload. if your pipeline requires <2min we will run a quick benchmark and report back.
[32:15] David Kim: on the SSO test — who will run it from Redwood side and what steps should our infra team expect? we want a repeatable checklist.

[33:00] Jordan Lee: Priya will lead the test. checklist will include exchange of metadata, provisional user account creation, test login, provisioning via SCIM, and role mapping verification. we'll include steps for AD federation specifics.
[36:40] Mark Thompson: any blockers we should be aware of? our timeline is to complete security validation in two weeks so we can move to pilot expansion.
[37:05] Priya Shah: nothing major; biggest risk is nested group mapping and log schema alignment, both of which we plan to address via the deliverables this week.

[40:55] Jordan Lee: quick recap — Redwood sends SAML metadata, SCIM examples, audit log sample, SOC 2 scope; Amberfield schedules SSO test and shares reviewers. we agreed on action owners and due dates.
[42:10] Elena Ruiz: sounds good. please mark which artifacts require an NDA or secure transfer so we loop legal.
[44:10] Jordan Lee: will do. thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with links. meeting adjourned.
